title: Dark Energy Camera Captures Galaxies in Lopsided Tug of War, a Prelude to Merger
caption: The galaxies NGC 1532 and NGC 1531, imaged by the Dark Energy Camera on the Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope
celestial: NGC 1532 · constellation Eridanus · about 55 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: CTIO/NOIRLab/DOE/NSF/AURA · Image processing: R. Colombari, M. Rodriguez, M. Zamani & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The spiral galaxy NGC 1532, also known as Haley's Coronet, is locked in a one-sided tug of war with a smaller neighbour, the dwarf galaxy NGC 1531, in this view from the Dark Energy Camera. The pair lie about 55 million light-years away in the direction of Eridanus.

The image captures the pull each galaxy exerts on the other as a massive galaxy and a dwarf galaxy move toward a merger. The contest is uneven, since the larger galaxy's gravity dominates, but the dwarf still leaves its mark, because interactions like this can distort a spiral's arms and stir up star formation.

Encounters between a large galaxy and a dwarf companion are thought to be one way big galaxies grow over time. The picture was taken with the US Department of Energy's Dark Energy Camera (DECam), which works on the NSF Víctor M. Blanco 4-meter Telescope, located at Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory in Chile.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (18.50 x 16.31 arcminutes) and distance (55 million light years), the frame spans roughly 296,000 × 261,000 light-years. Its light set out about 55 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Taken with DECam on the Blanco 4-meter Telescope through g, r and i filters. The colour mapping isn't published.
